title: Worksheet — Oceans and Continents (Class 6 CBSE)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions. Show working / write full answers for the subjective questions. Total time: 30 minutes.

questions.question: About what percentage of Earth's surface is water?
The largest ocean on Earth is the ____ Ocean.
The Sahara desert is in which continent?
Name the 7 continents in order from largest to smallest.
questions.answer: 1. Asia, 2. Africa, 3. North America, 4. South America, 5. Antarctica, 6. Europe, 7. Australia.

questions.question: Name the 5 oceans and where each is roughly located.
questions.answer: Pacific (between Asia/Australia and the Americas — largest); Atlantic (between Americas and Europe/Africa); Indian (south of Asia); Southern (around Antarctica); Arctic (around the North Pole — smallest).

questions.question: Match each feature to its continent: Himalayas, Amazon rainforest, Sahara desert, Great Barrier Reef.
questions.answer: Himalayas → Asia. Amazon rainforest → South America. Sahara desert → Africa. Great Barrier Reef → Australia.

questions.question: Name the oceans bordering Africa AND the seas (or bays) bordering India.
questions.answer: Africa: Atlantic Ocean (west) + Indian Ocean (east). India: Bay of Bengal (east) + Arabian Sea (west) + Indian Ocean (south).
questions.explanation: Africa has 2 oceans; India has 2 named arms of the Indian Ocean plus the open Indian Ocean.

questions.question: Why does most of India experience hot summers? Use the heat-zone idea.
questions.answer: The Tropic of Cancer (23½° N) passes through the middle of India. The area between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn is the TORRID Zone — the hottest part of the Earth, where the sun is overhead twice a year. Most of India lies in or just north of this zone, so it experiences strong, direct sunlight and hot summers. The land directly north of the tropic still has hot summers because the sun's angle is still high.
questions.explanation: Connects Tropic of Cancer to climate.

questions.question: Compare Antarctica and Australia in size, climate, and population. (5-6 sentences.)
questions.answer: Size: Antarctica is larger than Australia (5th-largest vs smallest). Climate: Antarctica is the COLDEST continent (almost entirely covered in ice); Australia is mostly hot and dry, with some tropical regions. Population: Antarctica has NO permanent population (only research stations); Australia has tens of millions of people across major cities. Both are in the southern hemisphere, but they are dramatically different in nearly every other respect — temperature, settlement, wildlife, and human history.
